statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-53057 is an Oracle Java SE Security (java.security) issue from the October 2025 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8360937 ("Enhance certificate handling"). The fix changes how X.509 distinguished names are parsed and rendered (sun.security.util.DerValue and sun.security.x509.AVA): before 21.0.9, BMPString values containing surrogate characters were accepted, and the RFC 2253 string forms decoded PrintableString, IA5String, T61String and BMPString values as UTF-8 regardless of their encoding. The flaw is in OpenJDK code, so every OpenJDK build (Temurin, Corretto, Zulu, Oracle) before 21.0.9 is affected. The Docker image versions were read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9+10, and later images ship 21.0.10 or newer. The Windows installer versions were read from the install4j jreBundle setting at each release tag: 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 bundle jdk-21.0.8+9, and 5.1.0 and later bundle 21.0.10 or newer.
statements.impact_statement: The Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 Docker images and the 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 Windows installers ship an affected runtime (Temurin 21.0.8); Docker images from 5.0.2 and installers from 5.1.0 ship Temurin 21.0.9 or newer and include the fix. The flawed code is present in that runtime; this assessment is that an attacker cannot exploit it through Liquibase Secure. Before 21.0.9, X500Principal.getName() in the RFC 2253 and canonical forms decoded name values as UTF-8 regardless of their ASN.1 string type, so a certificate name could render as text it does not contain. Liquibase Secure only acts as a TLS client, so the only certificate names it receives from a peer are those of the server certificates it validates. Path validation verifies every signature with the issuing CA's key, so a name can only reach any code in the process that reads it (the JDK's hostname verification, a bundled JDBC driver's own host name check, or Liquibase code) in a certificate signed by a CA the client trusts. Chain building and name constraints compare names in the affected canonical form, but a colliding issuer name only selects a candidate CA whose key must still verify the signature, and a subject that collides into a permitted subtree must still be signed by the constrained CA itself. Exploitation therefore requires a trusted CA to sign a server certificate with a deliberately malformed name. Publicly trusted CAs may not issue such certificates under the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, and an attacker able to get a trusted private CA to sign a certificate can already issue a valid one for the host, so the flaw adds nothing to that position. The JDK's own hostname verification reads SAN entries and the CN through DerValue.getAsString(), which decodes correctly. Liquibase code reads a certificate name only in DaticalTrueLicenseService, to display the holder of a license file that Liquibase signs.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Libraries (core-libs) issue, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8359454 ("Enhance String handling"). The Java version was read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and later ship 21.0.9 or newer. The fix changes a single branch of java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.insert(int, CharSequence, int, int): the one taken when the inserted sequence is a String and only part of it is inserted. A whole String now goes through the existing putStringAt(int, String) path, which copies the same bytes as the code it replaced, so the behaviour that changed is limited to inserting a sub-range of a String. A bytecode scan of the 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images found no caller of that form. In the JRE's lib/modules, no class other than StringBuilder, StringBuffer and AbstractStringBuilder references the four-argument insert. Across all jars under /liquibase, including nested jars and the license-tracking application, its only caller is the shaded ICU class CollationIterator$SkippedState in liquibase-checks.jar, which inserts a StringBuilder, not a String. The callers of insert(int, CharSequence), which forwards the whole sequence, are in shaded ICU and the DB2 JDBC driver and insert either a StringBuilder or a whole sequence. The changed code is therefore not executed by Liquibase Secure.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE whose cacerts still trusts the emSign roots the compromised intermediates chain to. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which deletes every emSign and Comodo AAA root from cacerts; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE and OpenJDK (component: HotSpot compiler) affecting OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, including Java SE 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1, 8u511-perf, and the corresponding GraalVM releases. Known as Java4Shell. On x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI, the JIT-compiled java.util.Base64 decoder miscomputes the output length for malformed padded input and writes up to 62 bytes past the end of the output array. An unauthenticated attacker who can send Base64 data to an application's decoder can corrupt the heap, leak heap memory and, with an exploit built for the application, execute code.
statements.action_statement: Liquibase Secure images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21 JRE (21.0.13 or earlier) that contains the vulnerable Base64 decoder. No Temurin release with the fix is available yet. Practical exposure is low for inbound attacks. Liquibase is a short-lived command-line process that accepts no inbound connections, and the Base64 data it decodes (license files, changelogs, loadData values) comes from the user. The published server exploits need many crafted requests to one long-running JVM, to warm up the decoder and arrange the heap. The remaining path is outbound: the researchers report a client-side exploit against a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server, so a run that connects to a database or service an attacker controls or impersonates may be exposed. Applications that embed the Liquibase libraries run on their own Java runtime and are affected through that runtime. Only x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake and newer Xeon, AMD Zen 4 and newer) are affected; ARM64 is not.

The JDK opens either a font file passed to Font.createFont or a font that fontconfig lists from the system font directories, owned by root, or from per-user font directories that only the account running Liquibase can write. No class in the jars shipped in the 5.0.0 through 5.1.1 images calls Font.createFont. The image's only installed fonts are the DejaVu TrueType fonts under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu, which are static fonts with no fvar, HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table. The container entrypoint runs only the Liquibase CLI and the optional lpm helper, a statically linked Go binary.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE JAXP partial denial-of-service issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. The matching OpenJDK fix is most likely JDK-8384031 (Enhance XML Processing), which replaces the linear namespace-prefix lookup in the Xerces parser with an indexed one, so a document with very many namespace declarations no longer costs quadratic time. Liquibase's XML changelog parser is namespace-aware, so the code is reachable, but only with the changelog files Liquibase is told to run. Whoever can change those files can already run arbitrary SQL against the target database, so slowing the parser gives an attacker nothing they do not already have, and the process is a short-lived command-line run, not a shared service.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE) affecting Oracle Java SE 8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1 and the corresponding GraalVM releases. The private keys of eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised, so an unauthenticated network attacker can present certificates the runtime accepts for any host and intercept or modify TLS traffic.
statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE that still trusts the compromised eMudhra intermediates. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which adds the 48 fingerprints from the upstream fix (JDK-8395142) to lib/security/blocked.certs; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. Until you upgrade, add the fingerprints to the bundled JRE's blocked.certs.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: 2D). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u503, 8u503-perf, 11.0.32.1, 17.0.20.1, 21.0.12.1, 25.0.4.1, 27; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20.1 and 21.0.12.1; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19.1.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition as well as unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data and unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE 2D issue (the graphics, imaging and font rendering subsystem). Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ships a Temurin 21 JRE between 21.0.8 and 21.0.12.1, which is in Oracle's affected range, so the version alone does not rule it out. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Liquibase Secure is a command-line tool that does not render images or fonts or decode untrusted image data. Liquibase's own code references only java.awt.Desktop, which hands a generated report to the local browser after an interactive run and is skipped when Liquibase's headless setting is on. That call passes a file path to the operating system and does no 2D rendering. A scan of the bundled jars for java.awt and javax.imageio references found these other users, none of which Liquibase passes image or font data to: browser-based sign-in helpers in the cloud and JDBC drivers (Desktop only), the H2 and HSQLDB GUI tools, geometry conversion helpers in the Databricks driver and Apache Commons Math, JAXB's image binding (Liquibase's JAXB models have no image fields), and the bundled data redaction library's PDF/image path, which uses ImageIO and Java 2D but is never run because Liquibase Secure calls that library only with plain text.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE ImageIO issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Oracle lists 21.0.12.1 as the last affected Java 21 release. The published Liquibase Secure images ship Temurin JRE 21.0.9 (5.0.2, 5.0.3), 21.0.10 (5.1.0, 5.1.1), 21.0.11 (5.2.0, 5.2.1), 21.0.12 (5.2.2) and 21.0.12.1 (6.0.0), so every one of them carries the vulnerable version. Exploitation requires an attacker to supply image data to the javax.imageio APIs. Liquibase reads changelogs, SQL and configuration, not images, and a source review found no use of javax.imageio in Liquibase code. The only ImageIO caller in the shipped code is the PDF redaction path of the policy-checks text filter (in 5.1.0 and later), which handles binary PDF documents; Liquibase only ever calls that filter's plain-text entry point, so the PDF and image code is never run. A scan of the bundled jars found one other ImageIO user, the JAXB runtime, which calls ImageIO only for JAXB-bound fields of type java.awt.Image; no class in the distribution binds such a field. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Oracle Java SE Networking issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Oracle does not say which OpenJDK change fixes this CVE, and the October update has several Networking fixes: SOCKS5 handshake length checks, the FTP and SMTP clients, and the java.net.http.HttpClient chunked response parser, redirect and authentication caching, and download file names. Liquibase Secure makes outbound HTTPS requests with the JDK's built-in HTTP client, and database drivers may use a SOCKS proxy when one is configured, so a malicious or intercepted HTTPS endpoint could reach some of this code. This is recorded as affected. The impact is limited to low integrity.

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Lightweight HTTP Server (com.sun.net.httpserver) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Oracle lists 21.0.12.1 as the last affected Java 21 release. The published Liquibase Secure images ship Temurin JRE 21.0.9 (5.0.2, 5.0.3), 21.0.10 (5.1.0, 5.1.1), 21.0.11 (5.2.0, 5.2.1), 21.0.12 (5.2.2) and 21.0.12.1 (6.0.0), so every one of them carries the vulnerable version. Exploitation requires an attacker to send requests to an HTTP server built on that API. Liquibase itself never starts an HTTP server: a source review found no use of com.sun.net.httpserver or any other listening socket in Liquibase code outside its tests, the images declare no exposed ports, and their entrypoint only runs the Liquibase CLI. Three bundled libraries do start a com.sun.net.httpserver listener, to receive the redirect of an interactive browser sign-in: the Microsoft authentication library (Azure interactive sign-in), the Databricks driver's OAuth browser flow and the Snowflake driver's OAuth authorization-code flow. These run only when a user configures one of those sign-in methods (Liquibase's Azure extension itself uses only Azure's default credential chain, which has no interactive browser sign-in). The listener is bound to the loopback interface and lives only while the user completes sign-in, so an attacker would need to send requests from the same machine during that window. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Oracle Java SE JSSE (TLS) certificate validation issue (CWE-295) from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Oracle does not say which OpenJDK change fixes this CVE. The most likely candidate is JDK-8382178 (Enhance TLS certificate handling), which reworks how the JRE enforces its CA distrust policies when validating server certificates. Certificate validation runs on every HTTPS and TLS JDBC connection Liquibase makes, and a certificate validation flaw is what an attacker on the network path between Liquibase and its database or service would use, so this is recorded as affected. The impact is limited to low integrity, and exploitation is hard.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later if you use Kerberos authentication. Oracle Java SE JGSS (Kerberos) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Unlike the sandbox-only JGSS issues CVE-2026-91463 and CVE-2026-91464, this one can be exploited by supplying data to the Kerberos APIs. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Oracle does not say which OpenJDK change fixes this CVE; the candidates are the three Kerberos client fixes in 21.0.13, JDK-8387217 (Enhance krb5 client), JDK-8387238 (Enhance Kerberos validation) and JDK-8387152 (Enhance krb5 tokens). This code runs only when Kerberos authentication is configured, for example MongoDB GSSAPI or Kerberos sign-in for SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL through JDBC. Those are supported configurations, so users who enable them are affected; an attacker would need to interfere with the Kerberos exchange, for example from the network path to the KDC or database. Users who do not configure Kerberos never run this code.

Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. This vulnerability does not apply to Java deployments, typically in servers, that load and run only trusted code (e.g., code installed by an administrator).

statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE Compiler (HotSpot C2 JIT) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update, affecting Java 11, 17, 21 and later. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Of the two C2 fixes in OpenJDK 21.0.13, JDK-8390400 (Enhance C2 comparisons, which corrects how compiled x86 code returns the old value of a byte or short compare-and-swap) is the one also backported to Java 17, so it matches this CVE's version list. The JIT compiles all code, so the flaw cannot be ruled out by reachability. Exploitation needs an attacker to supply data that drives a specific compiled code path in a long-running service that processes attacker requests. Liquibase Secure is a short-lived command-line process that accepts no inbound connections and processes changelogs and settings supplied by its operator.
